{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=formal+models+of+research+agenda+abandonment+in+science+and+autonomous+discovery&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6820898\", \"title\": [\"Formal Guarantees for Trustworthy Autonomous Biological Discovery: A Dual-Process Control Framework\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Generative AI now proposes protein sequences and metabolic pathways faster than laboratories can validate them, yet autonomous biological discovery is stalled by an unaddressed trust deficit: in-silico predictions regularly diverge from in-vitro outcomes, and no formal framework exists to bound this gap. We introduce Verifiable Agentic Biotechnology (VAB), a theoretical framework built on three provable guarantees. First, conformal prediction converts point estimates of biological fitness into finite-sample confidence intervals, guaranteeing coverage of true physical fitness with probability at least 1α irrespective of model misspecification. Second, a dual-process Constrained Markov Decision Process routes designs between fast heuristics and expensive mechanistic verifiers, achieving exact computational savings (C 2-C 1)P(σ 1 ≤ τ) while bounding safety degradation at γP(σ 1 ≤ τ). Third, the in-silico to in-vitro reproducibility gap is formalized as a Wasserstein distribution shift, yielding a Distributionally Robust Optimization bound V * DRBO on wet-lab transferability. Each bound is validated on controlled proxy environments and, in the case of conformal prediction, on real protein sequence data. The framework's parameters-α, τ , and ρ-map directly onto regulatory variables, providing a path from ungoverned sequence generation to auditable biological design.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6820898\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1002/9783527855841.ch14\", \"title\": [\"Materials Agents for Autonomous Research\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/9783527855841.ch14\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 3, 17]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6797083\", \"title\": [\"Employment Latency: A Formal Framework for Autonomous Employment Infrastructure, Discovery Latency Resolution, and Point-of-Offer Compliance Integration\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper introduces Employment Latency as a formally defined structural construct describing the cumulative time, effort, and opportunity cost imposed on qualified individuals by the requirement to manually discover, evaluate, and apply for employment opportunities at each new search cycle, regardless of prior qualification, demonstrated capability, or established employment history. The construct is distinct from and not captured by established labour market concepts including frictional unemployment (Diamond, 1982; Mortensen and Pissarides, 1994), search frictions (Stigler, 1962; McCall, 1970), or information asymmetry in hiring (Spence, 1973; Akerlof, 1970). While those frameworks address marketlevel coordination failures and employer-side information problems, Employment Latency specifically addresses the individual-level structural burden of repeated manual search effort across employment cycles, which persists even in efficient markets with low frictional unemployment and high information quality. The paper defines three measurable dimensions of Employment Latency: Discovery Latency, the time cost of manually monitoring fragmented opportunity sources at each search cycle; Application Latency, the effort cost of repeatedly generating tailored application materials from the same underlying profile information; and Verification Latency, the post-offer delay imposed by compliance verification processes that duplicate prior institutional verification of the same individual. Drawing on the Compliance Latency Framework (Egbedayo, 2025a), which established compliance as a verifiable portable state rather than a repeated institutional process, this paper extends the latency framework to the employment domain and proposes the Employment Latency Resolution Framework as the structural response. The framework comprises three integrated components: continuous&nbsp;autonomous opportunity discovery, AI-powered autonomous application submission with configurable confidence thresholds, and point-of-offer integration with a portable compliance profile system. The paper presents cross-sector evidence of Employment Latency in the UK labour market, analyses the technical architecture of an autonomous employment agent implementing the framework, and discusses policy, commercial, and research implications. The autonomous employment agent architecture described is protected by a UK patent application filed at the Intellectual Property Office in May 2026 under reference Rainfame-EMP-2026.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6797083\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4337/9781785364884.00011\", \"title\": [\"Formal Networks: A New Research Agenda?\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4337/9781785364884.00011\"}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "3427c350f06dcbc940ff6aea2c855d327e600345794f4d66f726d93511092d98", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "question_abandonment", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6820898", "doi:10.1002/9783527855841.ch14", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6797083", "doi:10.4337/9781785364884.00011"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6820898", "https://doi.org/10.1002/9783527855841.ch14", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6797083", "https://doi.org/10.4337/9781785364884.00011"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
